name: The Messthetics
label: Dischord
lede: Fugazi's rhythm section spent a decade and a half apart, came back as an instrumental trio with a jazz guitarist nobody in punk had heard of, and ended up on the same label as John Coltrane.

eras.title: The rhythm section, reassembled
eras.text: Joe Lally and Brendan Canty had locked in together for sixteen years in Fugazi. After Fugazi's hiatus Canty scored films and TV and Lally moved his family to Rome. When Lally came home, they started playing again, with jazz guitarist Anthony Pirog as the unexpected addition.

years.h: Joe Lally comes home from Rome and plays Brendan Canty his tapes
years.p: Back in Washington, Joe Lally reconnects with Brendan Canty and plays him his solo recordings. Canty suggests a guitarist: [[Anthony Pirog|10cb88bd-8490-4ebd-b311-fdc4a6530ee2]], a D.C. player from the jazz and experimental side of town.

years.h: Hired as Anthony Pirog's backing band, signed by Dischord
years.p: Lally and Canty first gather as Anthony Pirog's rhythm section for a project headed to [[John Zorn|7ec4a553-73e5-4c0d-a071-a82b83a309e6]]'s Tzadik label. The jams click, and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] comes to their first show and offers the trio a Dischord release instead.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the chemistry was immediate once the three started playing. MacKaye, who had shared a stage with both Lally and Canty for sixteen years in Fugazi, was in the room for the Messthetics' first gig and made the offer that turned a side project into a Dischord band.

It was a homecoming of sorts for Canty, whose [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] records came out on Dischord in the mid-'80s, and a new world for Pirog, whose own records had come out on jazz and experimental labels.

eras.title: Two hundred shows and a louder second record
eras.text: An instrumental band built from a punk rhythm section and a jazz guitarist had no obvious audience. The Messthetics found one the Fugazi way, by touring, and the second album, Anthropocosmic Nest, was built on what the road taught them.

years.h: The Messthetics, cut live in a practice space · Dischord No. 186
years.p: Nine instrumentals recorded live over 2017 in Brendan Canty's practice space, mostly without overdubs. Critics reached for labels like jazz punk jam.
years.xp: No vocals, no studio polish, just three people in a room, per Dischord. The LP was pressed on clear vinyl and runs from Mythomania to The Weaver.

years.h: The Messthetics play more than 200 shows
years.p: After the debut the Messthetics tour the U.S., Europe and Asia, playing more than 200 shows, according to Dischord. Two members of Fugazi, back in vans and clubs, playing songs with no words.

years.h: Anthropocosmic Nest, the road record · Dischord No. 189
years.p: Recorded in the Messthetics' practice space over 2019 to catch the live band: eleven tracks of improvised tangents, from Better Wings to Touch Earth Touch Sky.
years.xp:
Dischord pitched it as the record that finally caught the trio as it sounded on stage after two years of touring. Brendan Canty mixed it and [[TJ Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] mastered it; LP, CD and digital went out through Dischord's own store.

Bandcamp picked it among the best punk of September 2019.

eras.title: A tenor saxophone and the house that Coltrane built
eras.text: The Messthetics left Dischord for Impulse! Records, the jazz label that released A Love Supreme. With tenor saxophonist James Brandon Lewis out front, the trio became a quartet on record and on tour.

years.cap: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis, Impulse!, 2024
q: It's like a well-oiled machine playing with them.
years.h: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis on Impulse!
years.p: Nine tracks with saxophonist James Brandon Lewis, cut at Tonal Park in D.C. with producer Don Godwin, from L'Orso to Fourth Wall. Stereogum made it album of the week and Spin gave it an A−.
years.xp:
Dischord introduces James Brandon Lewis as an acclaimed jazz tenor saxophonist, composer and bandleader. He talked about Lally, Canty and Pirog the way jazz musicians talk about elders, telling interviewers that playing with them gave him a road education you can't get in school.

Dischord carries the album in its store as a distributed release.

years.h: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis, "Emergence"
yt: The Messthetics and James Brandon Lewis, "Emergence"

years.h: Deface the Currency, the second album with James Brandon Lewis
years.p: Announced in January 2026 with a tour, the Messthetics' second Impulse! album with James Brandon Lewis has seven tracks.
years.xp: It closes with Serpent Tongue (Slight Return), a new take on Serpent Tongue from the band's 2018 Dischord debut.
